hot.headline: Spotify is expanding audiobooks to more than 180 markets and says its Audiobooks+ add-on has passed $100M in annual recurring revenue
hot.kicker: Spotify said more than 750 million people will be able to stream or buy books on its platform once the rollout is complete. Source
hot.author: Mandy Dalugdug
hot.body:
Spotify ‘s audiobooks add-on, Audiobooks+ , has passed USD $100 million in annual recurring revenue just over a year after its launch.
The company disclosed the milestone at the Frankfurt Book Fair on Wednesday (October 7), where it also announced plans to take audiobooks from 22 markets to more than 180 by the end of 2026.
The new markets include Japan , India , South Korea , Indonesia , and Brazil . Spotify said more than 750 million people will be able to stream or buy books on its platform once the rollout is complete.
Audiobooks+ lets users pay for extra hours of audiobook listening on top of their plan, and has more than 1 million subscribers, a milestone Spotify first reported in May.
Spotify has pointed to the add-on as the first payoff from a strategy it laid out at its Investor Day that month: getting its most engaged users to pay more through add-ons.
Co-CEO Alex NorstrÃ¶m told investors that Spotify had expected music to be its first add-on, but that it was “our newest vertical, audiobooks, that got there first.” He added that Audiobooks+ subscribers have “lifetime values that are multiples of Premium-only users,” because they spend more and stay longer.
NorstrÃ¶m also said Spotify had taken roughly 20% of the US audiobooks market within a couple of years.
Listening is growing too. Monthly audiobook listeners on Spotify grew by nearly 40% over the past year, while listening hours rose by more than 30% , the company said.

Tom DeLonge of blink-182 at San Diego Padres game. CREDIT: K.C. Alfred / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images
Tom DeLonge has been spotted getting visibly emotional at a baseball game, after the crowd came together to sing Blink-182 ‘s ‘All The Small Things’.
The moment took place at San Diego’s Petco Park on Tuesday night (October 6), when the San Diego Padres went head to head against the Milwaukee Brewers in the third game of the National League Division Series.
DeLonge is a lifelong fan of the Padres, and recent years alone have seen him invited to throw out a ceremonial first pitch for their Wild Card Series opener back in 2024, and also gift catcher Kyle Higashioka one of his guitars later that year (via Heavy ).
Now, at the knockout game against the Brewers – where the Padres clinched a 4-3 victory – the pop-punk icon was spotted sitting in the audience, and got noticeably moved when the crowd sang his 1999 Blink-182 hit song ‘All The Small Things’.
During the rendition, FOX Sports captured the singer and guitarist nodding along and smiling as the audience sang, before later joining in and waving a yellow towel. Check it out below.
🎸 @blink182 's @tomdelonge in attendance tonight as Petco Park sings "All The Small Things" during Game 3 🎶 pic.twitter.com/d5sOPKJVws
For the Padres, the win over the Brewers came as they had to play without All-Star Mason Miller – who is out on paternity leave – as well as pitcher Adrian Morejon, who is temporarily out of action due to a shoulder injury.

The film “Cattle Run” has finally confirmed its theatrical release date five years after wrapping production in 2021!
A remake of Grímur Hákonarson’s film “Rams,” “Cattle Run” follows two estranged brothers who have not spoken a word to each other in 30 years. When a crisis strikes their village, the brothers put aside their differences to protect a calf named Jang Soo, whose birth seems almost fated amid the unfolding crisis.
Ryu Seung Ryong plays Man Soo, an older brother who is stoic only toward his younger brother.
Park Hae Joon plays Byung Soo, a younger brother who is prickly only toward his older brother.
Ong Seong Wu joins the cast as Jung Hoon, a rookie veterinarian newly assigned to Hoengsan County who finds himself caught between the two feuding brothers.
In the newly released stills, Man Soo gazes intently at the cows inside the barn. His serious yet gentle expression reflects his deep bond with the animals after years of running the Jung family ranch.
By contrast, Byung Soo looks noticeably prickly as he puts up a sign reading “The Original Jung Family,” seemingly all too conscious of his older brother.
Another still shows Jung Hoon sitting beside the calf with the bright expression of a rookie, hinting at the enthusiastic energy he will bring as a newly appointed veterinarian in Hoengsan County.

“A Love Other Than Yours” has unveiled a glimpse of the changed atmosphere between longtime couple Seo Kang Jun and Ahn Eun Jin !
KBS 2TV’s “A Love Other Than Yours” is a realistic romance drama that follows a couple in their 10th year of dating as they experience unexpected emotional changes in a relationship that once felt familiar.
In the previous episode, Namgoong Ho (Seo Kang Jun) learned the truth about what happened between Lee Mi Do (Ahn Eun Jin) and Han Tae Seung (Lee Joo Ahn) on the snowy night when Lee Mi Do had insisted that “nothing happened.” After 10 years of trusting each other, the unexpected revelation left Namgoong Ho deeply shaken.
Lee Mi Do has always been more than just a girlfriend to Namgoong Ho. When he was seven, she held his hand and ran away with him when loan sharks came after him. As a teenager, she cleared his name after his mother lied and shifted the blame onto him for her fraud. More recently, she protected him from loan sharks who showed up at his workplace. Having always been there to save him, Lee Mi Do is someone Namgoong Ho considers “the greatest hero in my life.”
However, the newly released stills show Namgoong Ho staring at Lee Mi Do with a cold, hardened expression, with his sense of betrayal evident in his eyes. Meanwhile, Lee Mi Do keeps her gaze lowered as she struggles with complicated emotions. In the preview for the upcoming episode, Namgoong Ho confronts her, saying, “You said nothing happened. You said there was nothing to worry about,” before asking, “How much more pitiful do you have to make me before you’re satisfied?,” revealing just how deeply he has been hurt.

Ice Spice has the internet locked in after she shared steamy photos from her Iceland vacation with actress and friend Millie Bobby Brown.
On Monday (Oct. 5), the Bronx rapper jumped on her Instagram account and posted a carousel of photos from her vacation in Reykjavik, Iceland, jokingly captioning the post "spiceland." Most of the pics featured the "In Ha Mood" rhymer wearing a silver-colored bikini posing against Iceland's moody, foggy mountain and watery backdrop. Spice confirmed that her pal Millie Bobby Brown took the photos.
In other images, Spice hangs out with friends of the Stranger Things actress, who also shared vacation pics she took on her IG account. The British thespian traveled to Iceland with her husband Jake Bongiovi and several friends, including Ice Spice. The crew took part in a whale-watching trip, spent time fishing, hiked scenic mountain trails and chilled in the country's geothermal waters. Brown captioned her IG photos, "Find your people, hold them close!"
Some fans on social media were surprised to see Spice hanging out with Brown, but the pair have been close friends for quite some time. Their friendship became public in July of 2026 when they filmed a viral TikTok challenge together with Lil Yachty over Drake's Iceman hit "Shabang." Since then, the dynamic duo has been photographed shopping and club-hopping in New York City.

warm.headline: Will Smith and DJ Jazzy Jeff’s Comeup Story Is Becoming a TV Show
warm.kicker: Al Pereira/Getty Images/Michael Ochs Archives
warm.author: Marisa Mendez
warm.body:
The story of how Will Smith and DJ Jazzy Jeff went from Philadelphia teenagers to one of hip-hop's first mainstream crossover acts is being developed into a TV show.
On Tuesday (Oct. 6), Deadline revealed Will's production company, Westbrook Studios, is developing a scripted series titled 215 , which will be inspired by Smith's early life and teenage years in Philadelphia's Wynnefield neighborhood. The series will follow a young rapper and DJ as they come up through the city's late 1980s and early 1990s hip-hop scene, pursue a record deal and navigate how fame affects their friendships and relationships with their hometown.
Will and Jeff first met at a house party in West Philadelphia in 1985. The two quickly began making music together and eventually formed DJ Jazzy Jeff & The Fresh Prince. Their 1988 album He's the DJ, I'm the Rapper became a major commercial success, helping establish the duo as one of hip-hop's earliest mainstream breakouts. And of course, Will would later become one of Hollywood's biggest stars.
" 215 is especially meaningful to us because it draws from the rise of DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince and celebrates Philadelphia during such a defining era in the city's late-'80s/early-'90s hip-hop scene,” Terence Carter, president of television at Westbrook Studios, said in a statement.
The series is still in development and does not yet have a network or streaming home, cast or release date. Westbrook Studios is developing the project in partnership with Canadian production company The Malar Group, which plans to produce several projects with the studio.

warm.headline: LL Cool J Challenges Rappers Who Think They’re Too Old to Rap
warm.kicker: What Now? With Trevor Noah/YouTube
warm.author: Marisa Mendez
warm.body:
LL Cool J believes artists who obsess over whether there's an "appropriate age" to make hip-hop are letting fear dictate what they can accomplish.
Sitting down for a new episode of What Now? With Trevor Noah published on Monday (Oct. 5), the rap legend discussed why longevity remains such a major talking point in hip-hop compared to genres like rock, where artists can continue performing well into their later years without their age becoming the focus.
For LL, he believes part of the reason is that hip-hop itself is still relatively young.
"It's a new genre," he explained. "The genre itself is so young. It's only 50-some years old itself as a genre."
The Queens native pointed out that many of hip-hop's pioneers are still active, meaning the culture is witnessing its earliest generations age in real time. But when it comes to artists questioning whether they can still make impactful music later in life, LL thinks fear is often the real culprit.
"Some people kind of obsess over, like, appropriate age to make hip-hop and all that," he said. "But I think the majority of [the] time, when you hear people obsessing over that, that's just fear talking."
LL challenged artists to stop dismissing older rappers and instead view longevity as a challenge.
"Don't say that it's not appropriate to be hot at a certain age now because you really just afraid you can't do it anymore,” he said.
The veteran rapper also reminded artists that aging doesn't mean losing their audience.

warm.headline: Suno hires Ticketmaster’s Michael Chua to lead its live music team, including Songkick
warm.kicker: In the role, Chua will lead the AI music company's live music operations, which include concert discovery platform Songkick. Source
warm.author: Music Business Worldwide
warm.body:
Suno has hired Michael Chua from Ticketmaster as Vice President and General Manager of Suno Live Experiences.
In the role, Chua will lead the AI music company’s live music operations, which include concert discovery platform Songkick .
Suno acquired Songkick from Warner Music Group in November 2025 , as part of the licensing agreement that settled WMG’s copyright lawsuit against the company.
Chua says he sees an opportunity at Suno to help artists “take a song from the first idea to the stage, and bring their fans along the whole way.”
According to Suno , the live experiences team will work on connecting Songkick’s discovery platform with what Suno calls its “creative entertainment platform.”
The team will also look to improve Songkick ‘s concert recommendations so that fans attend more shows, the company said.
“As Suno builds tools that help musicians create, reach fans and build lasting careers, live music has to be part of that,” said Chua . “I see an incredible opportunity at Suno to help artists take a song from the first idea to the stage, and bring their fans along the whole way.
“Bringing Suno and Songkick together opens up new possibilities to better connect artists and fans and ultimately create entirely new experiences that couldn’t have existed before Suno’s industry-leading tools.”
Chua joins Suno from Ticketmaster , a division of Live Nation Entertainment , where he was Vice President of Global Business Development and Strategic Partnerships.

warm.headline: Five-time Grammy winner Drake did not submit any of his three 2026 albums for consideration – joining BTS and Stray Kids in sitting out the 2027 awards (report)
warm.kicker: Sources told Billboard that the rapper did not submit any songs from Iceman, Habibti, and Maid of Honour to the Recording Academy. Source
warm.author: Mandy Dalugdug
warm.body:
Drake did not submit any of his three 2026 albums for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards , according to Billboard .
Sources told Billboard that the rapper also did not submit any songs from Iceman , Habibti , or Maid of Honour to the Recording Academy .
Billboard reported the detail on Monday (October 5) , in a feature examining hip-hop’s chances in the Grammys’ general field categories.
Drake released the three albums simultaneously on May 15 via Republic Records / Universal Music Group .
The trio took the top three spots on the Billboard 200 in their debut week, with Iceman at No. 1, Habibti at No. 2, and Maid of Honour at No. 3.
No act had done that before in the chart’s weekly history, which dates back to March 1956 .
Iceman earned 463,000 equivalent album units in the US in its first week, giving Drake his 15th Billboard 200 No. 1.
Billboard ‘s report noted that, as of September, Drake was the only rapper to have reached the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 as a lead artist in 2026.
The publication also pointed out that the Hot 100 dated October 25, 2025 , had no rap songs in its top 40 for the first time since February 1990 .
“This was a pretty weak year for standout [hip-hop] releases with storylines, with narratives,” Recording Academy member and record executive Riggs Morales told Billboard .
Billboard noted that Kendrick Lamar ; Clipse ; and Tyler, The Creator have no major releases eligible for the 2027 awards.

warm.headline: Warner Chappell Chair and CEO Guy Moot joins NMPA Board of Directors
warm.kicker: The NMPA announced Moot's appointment a week after he became sole chair of Warner Chappell on October 1. Source
warm.author: Rafaela Fornitani
warm.body:
Guy Moot , Chair and CEO of Warner Chappell Music , has joined the Board of Directors of the National Music Publishers’ Association ( NMPA ).
The NMPA is the US trade organization that represents music publishers and their songwriter partners.
The organization announced Moot ‘s appointment on Thursday (October 8), a week after he became sole chair of Warner Chappell on October 1.
“Guy Moot is one of the most distinguished creative and business minds in music,” said David Israelite , NMPA President and CEO. “From legends to emerging talent, he has a track record of identifying and championing incredible songwriters.
“The NMPA Board will benefit greatly from his perspective and expertise after over 30 innovative years in the industry.”
“Guy Moot is one of the most distinguished creative and business minds in music.”
“Standing up for songwriters’ rights has never been more critical, and David and his team at the NMPA are doing incredible work every day to lay the groundwork for our industry,” said Moot .
“I’m proud to join them and my colleagues on the Board as we continue protecting the true value of music and driving the future of publishing forward.”
Moot joins the board months after the NMPA announced industry-wide AI licensing deals with Udio and KLAY at its annual meeting in June.
Israelite said the Udio agreement was the first industry-wide licensing deal struck with a major AI music company, and the first to value songs and sound recordings equally for AI training.

Steve Martin and Alison Brown have turned it into a vintage-sounding bluegrass tune and recorded it with an all-star cast of singers and players from that genre, including two of the great living bluegrass vocalists, Del McCoury and Dan Tyminski. Chances are you won’t mind the song becoming an earworm again, now that it’s a multiple-banjo earworm, combining a high, lonesome sound from deep in the holler with (surprise) some of Martin’s contemporary comic flourishes.
On the eve of the song’s Thursday release, Variety talked via Zoom with Martin, who was taking a break from looping, and Brown, who was taking a break from banjo camp. Before recording this one-off, the duo was last heard from with last year’s collaborative album, “Safe, Sensible and Sane,” which included guests such as Jackson Browne. With “Old Town Road,” they really went all-in on an all-star roots ensemble, recruiting not just McCoury and Tyminski but Ronnie McCoury (Del’s son) on mandolin and harmonies, Stuart Duncan on fiddle and Garry West (Brown’s husband) on bass.
At the end of last year, Variety had a song the two of you did with Jackson Browne, “Dear Time,” on our list of 2025’s best songs last year. And now this is a very different kind of all-star track than “Dear Time,” to be sure. You came up with the “Old Town Road” arrangement, is that right, Alison?

warm.author: Walden Green
warm.body:
Third Man Records is reissuing Loretta Lynn ’s Van Lear Rose , the landmark 2004 comeback album Lynn made with Jack White . Out November 13 in vinyl and CD formats, the LP will also return to streaming services for the first time since it was mysteriously pulled in 2021. (Pitchfork has reached out to Third Man for more information.) To tide you over, you can now listen to the single “ Miss Being Mrs. ” on your platform of choice.
“It is an incredible honor to work again with Jack and his amazing team at Third Man to re-release this incredible album,” Patsy Russell, Lynn’s daughter, said in a press statement. “Our mother’s spirit lives on through this timeless music, and we are thrilled that fans old and new will be reminded of this great work.”
Lynn hadn’t released a solo album since 1988’s Who Was That Stranger when White coaxed her out of early retirement. Van Lear Rose went on to win two Grammys: Best Country Collaboration With Vocals, for the duet “Portland Oregon,” and Best Country Album. The new edition also features the bonus track “Just to Have You Back,” which chances are you’ve only heard if you bought the Third Man Vault reissue back in 2015.

warm.headline: Live Nation to sell $730M and €600M of bonds to refinance its 6.5% notes due 2027
warm.kicker: The new notes will retire the $1.2 billion of 6.5% debt Live Nation raised in May 2020, during the pandemic concert shutdown. Source

warm.body:
Live Nation Entertainment is selling USD $730 million and EUR â¬600 million of bonds.
The company intends to use the net proceeds to redeem all of its outstanding 6.500% senior secured notes due 2027 , to pay fees and expenses related to the offering, and for general corporate purposes.
Live Nation said those general corporate purposes “may include the repayment or repurchase of certain of the company’s indebtedness.”
Live Nation announced the pricing of the offering, which comprises senior notes due 2032 , on Wednesday ( October 7 ).
The dollar notes carry an interest rate of 7.125% a year, while the euro notes carry a rate of 6.125% .
Both tranches will be issued at 100% of face value, with the offering scheduled to close on October 15 , subject to closing conditions.
The final sizes differ from the terms Live Nation set out when it launched the offering on Tuesday ( October 6 ).
At launch, the company said it intended to offer USD $840 million of dollar notes and EUR â¬500 million of euro notes.
That means the dollar tranche was reduced by USD $110 million , while the euro tranche was increased by EUR â¬100 million .
The notes being redeemed date back to May 2020 , when Live Nation issued USD $1.2 billion of them, all of which were still outstanding at the end of June.
The bond sale comes as Live Nation continues to fight several legal battles in the US.
In April, a federal jury in Manhattan found that Live Nation and Ticketmaster had illegally monopolized primary ticketing at major US concert venues, and that Live Nation had monopolized the market for large amphitheaters, handing a win to a coalition of 33 states and the District of Columbia .

warm.headline: Elon Musk says Grok Bot will use Suno’s AI music models, alongside Anthropic’s Claude and Midjourney
warm.kicker: Suno does not currently offer an official public API. MBW reported in July that the company was exploring the launch of one. Source
warm.author: Mandy Dalugdug
warm.body:
Elon Musk says SpaceX ‘s AI agent, Grok Bot , will use models from AI music platform Suno .
Musk named Suno alongside Anthropic ‘s Claude Opus 5.5 and image generator Midjourney in a post on X on Wednesday (October 7) .
Grok Bot , which launched in beta in August , is an AI agent app developed by SpaceXAI .
SpaceXAI is the AI company Musk founded in 2023 as xAI , which SpaceX acquired in February and renamed in July . Musk said on October 4 that it will be renamed again, as SpaceXSI , but gave no date for the change.
Musk wrote: “Important note regarding Grok @Bot: Going forward, @SpaceX will use the best back end model for any given task, including Claude Opus 5.5, MidJourney, Suno and other leading APIs. Whatever is most likely to give you the best outcome.”
The post did not specify which tasks Grok Bot would route to which model, or when the change would take effect. In a follow-up post, Musk said simple questions would be routed to small, fast models and complex ones to large models.
For Claude , the change appears to be underway: a member of the Grok Bot team said on X that Opus 5.5 was rolling out and would power all Bots on the app. SpaceXAI has not said when music tasks will be routed to Suno .
Suno does not currently offer an official public API. MBW reported in July that the company was exploring the launch of one.
The company’s Chief Product Officer, Jack Brody , revealed those plans in a LinkedIn post on July 1 , with a form for developers to express interest.

warm.headline: David Byrne and Daniel Pemberton Made a Song Using Weird Elon Musk Quotes
warm.kicker: “Let Me Sell You a Dream” appears in Musk, a new documentary about the tech mogul directed by Alex Gibney
warm.author: Nina Corcoran
warm.body:
David Byrne and composer Daniel Pemberton are sharing a new collaborative song they made with a prompt that would make your creative writing professor happy. The lyrics to “Let Me Sell You a Dream,” their original track written for the upcoming Alex Gibney-directed documentary Musk , were created solely from Elon Musk quotes. (Byrne previously used this songwriting method on 2010’s Here Lies Love , where he similarly repurposed statements by Philippine First Lady Imelda Marcos.) Listen to the song below.
“It would be too easy and probably not as much fun to overtly criticize Musk,” said Byrne. “Better, I thought, to try and get inside his head a little bit, to use phrases he himself has used in interviews and statements, and let the character in the song be the one who describes himself.” The Talking Heads frontman also revealed that he arranged the lyrics and melody to “Let Me Sell You a Dream” before watching the movie, but accepted the offer because he was familiar with both Pemberton and Gibney’s work and thought it “sounded like fun.”
Musk is directed by Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alex Gibney, who also helmed Going Clear and The Inventor . The tech mogul declined to be interviewed for the documentary, so Gibney utilized Musk’s own words as recorded in podcasts, previous interviews, and outtakes from documentaries to shape his film about the CEO of Tesla, SpaceX, and X (formerly Twitter). It’s nearly four hours long and also features original interviews with Musk’s ex-partners, journalists, engineers, and others. Musk hits theaters nationwide on October 16.

warm.headline: Miley Cyrus’ new album ‘Bass Persuades’ makes US chart history as biggest drop from Number One debut
warm.kicker: The record has fallen 156 places on the Billboard 200 just one week after topping the chart The post Miley Cyrus’ new album ‘Bass Persuades’ makes US chart history as biggest drop from Number One debut appeared first on
warm.author: Max Pilley
warm.body:
Miley Cyrus receiving a Hollywood Walk Of Fame star on May 22, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
Miley Cyrus ’ new album ‘Bass Persuades’ has made US chart history after suffering the biggest-ever second-week drop for an album that debuted at Number One.
The singer – who now goes simply by Miley – released her 10th studio album last week and it entered the Billboard 200 at the summit with 61,000 equivalent album units, marking her first US Number One since 2013’s ‘Bangerz’.
A week later, however, it has plummeted 156 places to Number 157 – the biggest drop in Billboard 200 history for an album immediately following a Number One debut.
The only steeper falls were Bon Jovi ’s 2016 album ‘This House Is Not For Sale’, which returned to Number One in 2018 after being bundled with concert tickets, before falling to Number 169 the following week, and Travis Scott ’s 2014 mixtape ‘Days Before Rodeo’, which hit Number One a decade after its original release, before disappearing from the Billboard 200 entirely the next week.
‘Bass Persuades’ arrived on September 18 through Atlantic Records, just weeks after Miley announced the album alongside two Hollywood Bowl shows .
The announcement also confirmed that she would henceforth be billed simply as Miley, dropping ‘Cyrus’ from her professional name. Her father Billy Ray Cyrus later backed the change , saying: “I always called my little girl Miley. Just… Miley.”

Turnstile have announced a free show at the Washington Monument later this month, which will raise money for the people in Palestine, Sudan, and Lebanon.
The Baltimore hardcore giants announced the Washington D.C. performance today (Thursday October 8) on their social media channels, and confirmed that the one-off gig will start at 3pm local time on October 24.
At the show, they will perform by the historic monument and make entry completely free for visitors. It comes in collaboration with Human Concern International – and Turnstile have encouraged fans to donate on the day, with proceeds being “divided equally among its humanitarian efforts in Palestine, Sudan, and Lebanon”.
The newly-announced show will now mark the final date on their huge North American tour, which kicked off in June and comes in support of their 2025 album ‘ Never Enough ’.
“As a Gazan, I cannot be prouder of the Turnstile team and community for coming together to support the people of Gaza, Lebanon, and Sudan. Three regions who have suffered so much,” said Hassan Wadi, the global director of Human Concern International.
“With your support we aim to provide food, water, medical care, and shelter to families in need in all three regions. Thank you all for your support, we are honoured to collect and deliver these donations.”
The announcement of the free show comes on the heels of the hardcore icons speaking to NME at the 2026 BRIT Awards , and highlighting the importance of musicians using their platforms to speak out against injustice.

Thom Yorke performs at Sidney Myer Music Bowl on October 29, 2024 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Naomi Rahim/WireImage)
Thom Yorke has revealed that Radiohead ’s 2025 reunion tour led to a “massive” crash in his self-confidence that took months to recover from.
The band announced their long-awaited live return in September last year , marking their first shows together in over seven years. They went on to play 20 arena dates across Madrid, Bologna, London, Copenhagen and Berlin that November and December.
Now, in a new conversation with Harry Styles for Rolling Stone , Yorke has spoken about the more difficult aftermath of the comeback.
The subject arose as Styles asked him about becoming more willing to embrace and celebrate his past work, both through the Radiohead tour and by accepting the Academy Fellowship at the 2026 Ivor Novello Awards .
“You’re answering this better than I can do,” Yorke replied. “You’re right, that I’m in a slightly better place nowadays, but I’d be lying if I didn’t say that something like getting an Ivor Novello fellowship was not deeply confusing for me.
“I admire a lot of the people that they’ve given those awards to. Some of these people are my heroes. But I have a very, very strange relationship to… God, this is really hard to explain. I have a very strange relationship to that element of my work.”
“I find it hard to believe in it,” he continued. “The moving-forward thing, that’s what I believe in. That’s easy to believe in, because it’s new. I don’t have to explain it, so I’m happy.”

Blossoms have spoken to NME about the race for this week’s Number One against The Beatles and Johnny Marr with their latest album ‘Songs From The Wedding Cake’, as well as their mission to keep things DIY and handmade in the age of AI.
The Stockport indie veterans released their sixth album last week (Friday October 2), which found itself sandwiched in-between The Beatles’ ‘Rubber Soul’ reissue and The Smiths icon Marr’s new solo effort ‘The Age Of Everything ‘ at Number Two in the midweeks.

“Saying the wrong thing in an argument, losing your wife’s no claims bonus, crying at the Kardashians, it’s all in there,” he shared. “The album is named after Stockport Town Hall, which everyone round where we live calls the Wedding Cake, and it’s where I got married, so it couldn’t be much closer to home.

As this century progressed and the impact of the White Stripes and the Strokes — the last two rock bands who truly shaped culture — began to fade, the Grammy rock nominees reflected this conundrum, mixing aging classic rockers like Bruce Springsteen, U2, AC/DC, Tom Petty and even Led Zeppelin (who broke up in 1980 but won best rock album in 2014 for a reunion-concert recording of half-century-old songs) with newer classic rockers like Foo Fighters, Alabama Shakes and the Black Keys, throwing in relative newbies like Radiohead (who seem to be trying very hard not to be a rock band), Kings of Leon, Arctic Monkeys, Twenty One Pilots and Jack White. warm.headline: Björk’s ‘Orkestral’ World Comes Home On Live LP
warm.kicker: Björk is giving one of her most intimate recent concert projects a physical life.
warm.author: SPIN Staff
warm.body:
Björk is giving one of her most intimate recent concert projects a physical life. Björk Orkestral with the Hamrahlíð Choir , recorded at Reykjavík’s Harpa Concert Hall in October 2021, will receive its worldwide physical release Nov. 27 on LP, CD, Blu-ray and DVD.
The performance captures Björk reimagining her catalog through orchestration rather than spectacle, putting her voice, electronics and the contributions of Iceland’s Hamrahlíð Choir at the center. “I am so happy and proud of this concert,” Björk says. “We all put enormous love, energy and time into it.” She describes learning over the years about “the juxtaposition of voices and the electronic,” calling it a philosophical question of “how nature and technology can coexist amicably.”
That balance became especially important during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Harpa performances were conceived and rehearsed during that period, when the stripped-down Orkestral format allowed Björk to revisit older songs she felt she had not yet figured out how to perform live. Unlike the more elaborate visual worlds of the immersive Cornucopia , the Orkestral concerts put the architecture of the music itself front and center.
At the heart of the release is the Hamrahlíð Choir, conducted by its founder Þorgerður Ingólfsdóttir. The relationship between Björk and the choir goes back to Utopia ’s “Body Memory” and expanded through the Cornucopia live production, including its original New York run and subsequent European dates. The repertoire draws heavily from the vocal experiments of 2004’s Medúlla , while also reaching across Björk’s catalog.

warm.headline: Rosalía shares that Bono reached out for Spanish advice on U2 song about her: “Feel free to invent your own language”
warm.kicker: The band have written ‘The Mirror Maker (Rosalía)’ about her for their new album ‘Carnaval De Luz’ The post Rosalía shares that Bono reached out for Spanish advice on U2 song about her: “Feel free to invent your own lang
warm.author: Max Pilley
warm.body:
Rosalía has revealed that Bono reached out to ask for her help with some Spanish lyrics while working on U2 ’s forthcoming song about her.
The Spanish star discussed the unlikely exchange during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon last night (Wednesday October 7), explaining that she and the U2 frontman have still never met in person.
Their contact came while Bono was working on ‘The Mirror Maker (Rosalía)’, the fourth track on U2’s forthcoming album ‘Carnaval De Luz’ .
“I don’t know him personally, but he texted me and told me that he had this new project and this song, ‘The Mirror Maker’,” Rosalía told Fallon.
She said Bono then asked whether some of the Spanish words he had written actually made sense. Rosalía recalled being puzzled by one in particular, saying she had “never heard this word” and eventually researched it to discover that it did not exist in standard Spanish.
Her advice to Bono was straightforward: “I don’t know, but feel free to invent your own language.”
She went on to describe the entire situation as “mind-blowing”, adding that she had grown up listening to U2 and singing a snippet of ‘With Or Without You’.
Bono first revealed the story behind ‘The Mirror Maker (Rosalía)’ last month , describing the singer as an “extraordinary artist”.
“We normally just write songs about people in jail or dead people,” he joked at the time. “This is just celebrating somebody just because they’re an extraordinary artist.”

warm.author: Alex Suskind
warm.body:
Information continues to trickle out about Grand Theft Auto VI ahead of its hotly anticipated November 19 release. Today, Rockstar Games unveiled details around one of the long-running series’ best features: the in-game radio stations and their respective DJs.
GTA VI ’s programming will include Cocoteo FM, a modern Latin station hosted by Bad Bunny and RaiNao ; the best in African music on AfroBank FM, from Burna Boy and Palms Trax ; classic metal on Chamber 106.6, from Kerry King and Tom Araya of Slayer ; Flash FM’s “best in pop” led by Robyn and model Alex Consani; Dirty South Classics from Trick Daddy and Trina ; and Back Country Radio, the home of “renegade country,” led by Morgan Wallen , Lana Del Rey , and—in perhaps the game’s biggest coup—Lana’s husband, Jeremy Dufrene.
“Cocoteo gets our vibe, our slang, our taste, our pride, our experiences, our traditions, and all our crazy antics,” RaiNao said in a statement to Pitchfork. “It feels incredibly special to lend my voice to GTA VI and do it in the best way possible: having fun, embodying a character who’s like me, and putting our culture, our music, and our people in the spotlight.” The Puerto Rican artist added, “I was never extreme about video games, but GTA was one of my favorites…. Diving around in a stolen car, blasting music with all that adrenaline pumping was THE VIBE. It’s mind-blowing to know that I’ll now be part of that experience.”

warm.headline: Fierce, frantic and loaded with menace: Fontaines DC’s 20 greatest songs – ranked!
warm.kicker: Ahead of the Irish alt-rockers’ highly anticipated fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, we count down their potent, occasionally political, catalogue A single inspired by the birth of bassist Conor Deegan’s daughter, It’s Amaz
warm.author: Alexis Petridis
warm.body:
Ahead of the Irish alt-rockers’ highly anticipated fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, we count down their potent, occasionally political, catalogue
A single inspired by the birth of bassist Conor Deegan’s daughter, It’s Amazing to Be Young is a lovely example of Fontaines DC operating in euphoric mode, a relatively recent addition to their emotional mood board: “Sometimes,” offered frontman Grian Chatten , “optimism is a necessary delusion.”
It’s often cheeringly difficult to work out exactly what Fontaines DC’s influences are , but the shadow of Pixies definitely hangs over Romance’s Death Kink, from the string-bending lead guitar line on the chorus to the fabulously wonky solo and the abrupt ending. A delight, albeit one as dark-hued as the title suggests.
The best take on A Lucid Dream might be the radically different “live version” released as a single in 2021, which slows the tempo, drags a piano into proceedings and amps up the song’s ineffable sense of menace. That said, the original – speedy drums, abstract guitar noise, ferocious climax – is quite something, too.
As introductions to a new band go, the opening track of Fontaines DC’s debut album, Dogrel , takes some beating. Big is a fierce, snotty, swaggering, supremely exciting statement of intent (“Dublin in the rain is mine … I’m gonna be big”) that immediately lets listeners know they are in the presence of something special.

warm.headline: Yungblud Unveils Live Billy Corgan Collaboration
warm.kicker: It came one day before Yungblud made his first return in eight years to Lollapalooza, where the Smashing Pumpkins headlined the following night.
warm.author: SPIN Staff
warm.body:
Yungblud and Billy Corgan are taking their “Zombie” collaboration back to the stage — or, more precisely, back to the stage it was captured on this summer.
The British rocker has released “Zombie (Live From the Riviera Theatre),” a recording of his July 30 performance with the Smashing Pumpkins frontman at the famed Chicago venue. It marks the only time the pair have performed their reimagined version of the song together live. It came one day before Yungblud made his first return in eight years to Lollapalooza, where the Smashing Pumpkins headlined the following night.
“Zombie” first appeared on Yungblud’s chart-topping IDOLS , becoming the fastest-streaming single of his career and surpassing 200 million total streams. The song also earned a Grammy nomination for Best Rock Song. Yungblud later re-recorded the song with contributions from Corgan and fellow Smashing Pumpkins members Jimmy Chamberlin and James Iha in a nod to the influence of the band’s Siamese Dream on his own music.
It will also likely be his only new music in the short term: in August, Yungblud broke his leg in a motorcycle accident at the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally in South Dakota but still managed to make it through a handful of scheduled shows. He hasn’t been onstage Aug, 21, when he performed at Belgium’s Pukkelpop festival, although he did join a civilian for surprise duet on Bryan Adams’ “Heaven” at a Stockholm bar on Sept. 1.

warm.headline: Joe Strummer’s Pre-Clash 101’ers Era Gets Boxed
warm.kicker: An early chapter of the late Strummer’s musical life is getting the archival treatment it deserves.
warm.author: SPIN Staff
warm.body:
Long before Joe Strummer became one of the voices of the Clash, he was living in a London squat and playing pubs and clubs with a band named after the address where they lived. Now, that early chapter of the late Strummer’s musical life is getting the archival treatment it deserves.
The George Harrison-founded Dark Horse Records has announced Joe Strummer 003: The 101’ers Years , a definitive collection of studio and live recordings from Strummer’s pre-Clash band, due Nov. 20. The three-CD deluxe edition collects 48 tracks and comes housed in a 48-page hardback book with slipcase, while a two-LP edition will also be available.
The 101’ers formed in 1974 as a house band among the residents of 101 Walterton Road in Maida Vale, where Strummer and his fellow musicians were squatting. The group became fixtures on London’s burgeoning pub-rock circuit, mixing rock, R&B and rockabilly at pubs, clubs and squat benefits around the city.
“The Labour government introduced the Rent Act in 1965,” Strummer said previously. “Its purpose was to protect tenants in rented accommodation. Unfortunately, it backfired as most laws do — and the result was landlords found a loophole and switched to short lets, which were not covered. warm.headline: Steve Martin, Alison Brown Take ‘Old Town Road’ To Bluegrass Country
warm.kicker: What happens when one of the biggest crossover hits of the 21st century gets handed to a couple of banjo virtuosos?
warm.author: SPIN Staff
warm.body:
What happens when one of the biggest crossover hits of the 21st century gets handed to a couple of banjo virtuosos? Steve Martin and Alison Brown have the answer.
The pair have teamed up with bluegrass heavyweights Del McCoury, Dan Tyminski, Ronnie McCoury, Stuart Duncan and Garry West for a bluegrass reimagining of Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road,” out today (Oct. 8) in tandem with a humorous behind-the-scenes video. The track follows Martin and Brown’s 2025 album Safe, Sensible and Sane , which features guest turns from Vince Gill, the Indigo Girls and Jackson Browne.
“I’ve always loved the idea of ‘Old Town Road’ as seen through bluegrass eyes,” Martin says, while Brown adds, “it’s such a well-known song that my challenge was to come up with an arrangement that would showcase our banjos without giving the song away too soon.”
The solution was to go all the way in. Martin wrote new, “grass-ified” lyrics, while the arrangement swaps the original’s youthful, urban-leaning production for a full-on banjo-driven bluegrass romp. “Fortunately, some of the best bluegrass musicians in the world agreed to join us, and here we are, ready to ride,” Martin says.
The source material hardly needs an introduction. “Old Town Road” became a cultural event after its 2019 release, initially exploding on TikTok before crossing from hip-hop into country and pop on a scale that made genre boundaries look increasingly quaint. The remix featuring Billy Ray Cyrus spent 19 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, a record at the time that has since been tied by Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” and broken by Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas.”

Pacific Music Group (PMG) has launched a Tokyo office, PMG Japan , and signed Japanese rapper JP THE WAVY .
The rapper has joined PMG on a long-term 360 deal covering recorded music and management, the company announced today (October 8) .
PMG says JP THE WAVY is PMG Japan’s first major signing and that he will begin releasing new music through the partnership this fall.
PMG , which is headquartered in Hong Kong , was launched in November 2025 by NE-YO , Sonu Nigam , MC Jin , and Jonathan Serbin .
Serbin , PMG’s CEO, previously served as Co-President of Warner Music Asia , a post he was appointed to in 2021 .
According to PMG , the hub will cover artist development, recorded music, management, promotion, brand partnerships, and cross-border collaboration.
The company says the office will work in two directions: taking Japanese artists to audiences outside the country and bringing international acts to fans in Japan and across Asia.
For JP THE WAVY , PMG says its plans include growing his audience across Asia and pursuing opportunities in the United States and other Western markets.
Beyond recorded music and management, PMG says the deal also covers audience development, collaborations, live opportunities, and brand partnerships.
JP THE WAVY broke through in 2017 with his single Cho Wavy De Gomenne .
In 2021 , he teamed up with Good Gas on Bushido , from the official soundtrack to F9: The Fast Saga .

warm.headline: UK government shout out “shared European interest” of solving Brexit touring crisis in push for “real progress” in Brussels
warm.kicker: With over £1billion lost across the EU and more than 17,000 jobs, the UK government are calling on Europe to pull together to solve the UK's Brexit touring crisis for artists and crew The post UK government shout out “sh
warm.author: Andrew Trendell
warm.body:
Grace Kelly of Venus Grrrls performs at 2000 Trees 2026 (Photo by James Klug/Getty Images)
The UK government have highlighted the “shared European interest” in solving the ongoing Brexit touring crisis for artists, musicians and crew as they called for more “real progress” at an event in Brussels. See exclusive quotes from DCMS Minister Ian Murray’s speech below.
After the music industry were essentially dealt a “no deal” Brexit with an end to visa-free travel for UK artists and crew wishing to work back in 2020, “ catastrophic” predictions of the sector being “screwed over ” and facing an existential threat to the talent pipeline have come into fruition and remain unresolved.
A report by the Musicians’ Union in 2024 found that 75 per cent of artists had seen a decline in bookings in the EU since Brexit, with 79 per cent unable to make up for the loss of work elsewhere and the majority claiming that touring in Europe was simply “no longer financially viable”. A recent study by UK Music found that the impact of Brexit on touring was only “worsening” with the rate of growth down by more than half on 2023 – despite “record-breaking” income reported by the upper echelons.
Back in March, the Labour government pledged “full commitment ” to solving the crisis and breaking down barriers to musicians needing to tour Europe. June saw MPs share a new report calling for the government to work closely with the EU and individual member states to break down the problems and put a stop to the devastation being brought upon the live music music industry by Brexit.

warm.headline: Spiritland launches beautiful new London listening bar at The Barbican
warm.kicker: Opening later this month, it will feature album playbacks, regular talks, tastings, supper clubs and more The post Spiritland launches beautiful new London listening bar at The Barbican appeared first on NME .
warm.author: Liberty Dunworth
warm.body:
The Barbican has joined forces with Spiritland to launch a new listening bar in London.
Dubbed ‘Spiritland At The Barbican’, the new partnership comes in time for the 10th anniversary of its original Coal Drops Yard site, and will offer a daily programme of artists and record collectors playing a wide variety of genres.
Situated on Level 2 of the Barbican, with lakeside views overlooking the fountains, the genres on offer range from jazz to classical, and from ambient to electronica – each designed to complement and mirror the centre’s wider cultural programming.
Nightly listening sessions will also be available, as will regular talks, tastings, supper clubs and more. One of the more regular fixtures will be the 5pm album playbacks, which see a different album played in its entirety every day; whether it be a classic album from Bach, a more modern favourite from Beck, or a lesser-known gem from an emerging artist.
“The objective of this system is to present the artistry and eloquence of the musical performance – emotional communication is the key element in music and it is this that needs to be preserved and is the enduring ambition of the kit,” Kevin Scott of Living Voice, the soundsystem company that helps bring the listening bar to life.
Paul Noble of Spiritland shared that the Lakeside Room at the Barbican “is a stunning space for us to go even deeper into the music we love – jazz, soul, contemporary classical, ambient, electronica and more on an outrageously high end soundsystem”, and Beau Vigushin, Chief Experience Officer at the Barbican, described it as “yet another exciting reason to visit the Barbican”.

warm.headline: Dafydd Owain’s second album wins the 2026 Welsh music prize
warm.kicker: Ymarfer Byw, which was praised for its ‘musical excellence’, beat 14 other albums to the prize of £10,000 Singer-songwriter Dafydd Owain has won the 2026 Welsh music prize with his second album Ymarfer Byw. The emotional
warm.author: Michael Cragg
warm.body:
Ymarfer Byw, which was praised for its ‘musical excellence’, beat 14 other albums to the prize of £10,000
Singer-songwriter Dafydd Owain has won the 2026 Welsh music prize with his second album Ymarfer Byw.
The emotionally charged record, which also won Welsh language album of the year in August, beat albums by the likes of Gruff Rhys, the Royston Club and Art School Girlfriend to the prize of £10,000.
Receiving the award at Wales Millennium Centre in Cardiff on Wednesday, Owain, from Caernarfon, north-west Wales, told the BBC : “It’s just amazing, isn’t it? Such talented, amazing artists on the shortlist. There’s a multitude of people that contribute to creating any album, and it’s not a solo project, even though we call it a solo project … I just hope, if anything, this album and this award mean I’m able to create more music. But it’s such a privilege to win in such esteemed company.”
During his acceptance speech Owain spoke of his first performance at the same Cardiff venue as a 16-year-old choir member: “I mimed the whole thing because I was ... scared of making a bum note,” he recalled . “It’s weird to have an award for what’s essentially singing now.”
Huw Stephens, who co-founded the prize in 2011, praised Ymarfer Byw’s “musical excellence” and Owain’s “very personal and moving lyrics”.
Past winners of the award, now in its 16th year, include Gwenno, Kelly Lee Owens and Deyah. Producer Don Leisure took home last year’s award for his album, Tyrchu Sain.

warm.headline: LABOUM’s Yujeong Announces Marriage With Heartfelt Letter
warm.kicker: LABOUM’s Yujeong is tying the knot this coming winter! On October 8, Yujeong announced the happy news by posting a photo of a handwritten letter on her social media. In the letter, she wrote: Hello, this is Yujeong 🙂 Bac
warm.author: E Ezeji
warm.body:
On October 8, Yujeong announced the happy news by posting a photo of a handwritten letter on her social media.
Back in September 2021, I left you a handwritten letter after wrapping up my seven-year contract and concluding my activities with “LABOUM,” and it’s already been five years since I last wrote to you like this.
Since 2022, I’ve been hosting “K-FORCE SPECIAL SHOW”—a program that feels like family to LABOUM—and have continued to foster precious bonds with our military personnel. I’ve also met listeners as a special radio DJ, released music, traveled extensively—something I didn’t get to do much in my 20s—and fulfilled my small dream of living on my own, taking time to learn how to live at a more leisurely pace.
As I accumulated these new experiences one by one, I was gradually making my life a little more solid and fulfilling. 🙂
I’ve met a wonderful partner whom I’ve decided to spend the rest of my life with, and we’re now preparing to walk through the years ahead together.
I had always thought of myself as someone who had lived life bravely and independently on my own, but I met someone who cherishes me like his own daughter, makes me feel every day just how loved I am, and gives me a sense of comfort and security whenever we’re together.
Over the past year, we have been slowly and carefully preparing for our marriage at our own pace, and now I’m happy to finally share this joyful news with all of you.

The upcoming film “White Blast” has unveiled new stills featuring Kim Yun Seok and Koo Kyo Hwan !
“White Blast” is a mystery thriller film that follows the story of Gap Soo (Kim Yun Seok), a station master nearing retirement, and his newly appointed successor Hyun Taek (Koo Kyo Hwan), after they discover a mysterious body at a rural train station isolated by a heavy snowstorm.
The newly released stills feature a variety of scenes, from Gap Soo and Hyun Taek’s first meeting to the moment they discover a mysterious body during the handover.
In the photos, Gap Soo meets Hyun Taek, a new station employee who arrives through the heavy snow, as he prepares for his final shift at Seolo Station, which he has guarded throughout his career, and begins the handover.
In one still, Gap Soo holds a stack of documents and looks sharply at Hyun Taek.
In another, Hyun Taek carefully watches Gap Soo’s reaction as he hands over the walkie-talkie.
Gap Soo and Hyun Taek continue the handover on snow-covered tracks, cut off from the outside world and surrounded by an uneasy tension.
However, their quiet routine at Seolo Station is disrupted when they discover a mysterious body lying on the tracks.
Another still shows Inspector Choi ( Park Soo Young ), who has worked at the Seolo Police Substation for many years and grown close to Gap Soo, speaking with newly assigned Officer Yang (Roh Yoon Seo) with serious facial expressions. The still hints that an unsettling change is about to descend on Seolo Station.

warm.headline: Kang You Seok Is A Friendly Applicant Who Hides His Anxiety Behind A Smile In “Final Interview”
warm.kicker: The upcoming film “Final Interview” has unveiled new stills featuring Kang You Seok! “Final Interview” follows six applicants who make it to the final round of interviews at a global IT company amid an intensely competit
warm.author: MLim
warm.body:
The upcoming film “Final Interview” has unveiled new stills featuring Kang You Seok !
“Final Interview” follows six applicants who make it to the final round of interviews at a global IT company amid an intensely competitive job market. After discovering mysterious envelopes containing exposés about each of them at the final interview venue, the six begin to suspect one another and find themselves locked in a tense psychological battle.
Kang You Seok plays Lee Hee Chan, a friendly and witty applicant. Lee Hee Chan is a natural mediator who uses his cheerful personality and easygoing charm to ease the awkward atmosphere in the interview room. Although he desperately wants to land the job, he hides his anxiety behind a smile and remains calm even when faced with the daunting task of choosing the one person who will ultimately be hired.
Kang You Seok brings out Lee Hee Chan’s approachable charm while subtly building his character’s unexpected transformation as the mysterious envelopes appear and one revelation after another comes to light, adding to the tension and immersion of the film.
Kang You Seok shared his affection for the character, saying, “I was drawn to the fact that the six characters, each with their own secrets, clash within the confined space of an interview room.” He added, “To portray the subtle feelings hidden beneath Hee Chan’s bright exterior, I discussed the character extensively with the director and my fellow actors while preparing for the role.”

Lee Jun Hyuk , Seo Hyun Woo , and Oh Dae Hwan have shared key viewing points ahead of the finale of “ The Ordinary Jackpot ”!
Based on a webtoon, “The Ordinary Jackpot” follows Gong Eun Tae (Lee Jun Hyuk), an ordinary sales employee who wins the lottery jackpot. Though the prize—1.3 billion won (approximately $950,000)—isn’t quite enough to dramatically transform his life overnight, the experience ultimately inspires him to change himself instead. Rather than quit, he returns to work the very next day with a completely different outlook on life.
As the drama approaches its conclusion, the conflict between Sales Team 5, led by Gong Eun Tae, and Jung Sun Hyuk (Oh Dae Hwan), who has turned against them, continues through the final episodes.
Jung Sun Hyuk previously made a choice that turned him from a colleague of Gong Eun Tae and Sales Team 5 into an adversary, while a crisis was also foreshadowed for the entire Hongsung International. With the final two episodes approaching, the key question is what choices the members of Sales Team 5 will make as they balance their individual interests against the fate of their team.
Lee Jun Hyuk said, “It would be great if viewers could stay tuned to see what happens to Hongsung International and Sales Team 5 all the way to the end.” It remains to be seen what kind of conclusion awaits Gong Eun Tae, whose attitude toward life shifted after winning 1.3 billion won in the lottery, and how his journey will unfold alongside Sales Team 5.

warm.headline: 3 Situations That Felt Like A Battlefield In Episodes 7-8 Of “The Ordinary Jackpot”
warm.kicker: Some people might believe that money is the solution to every problem; however, it hasn’t been like that for Gong Eun Tae (Lee Jun Hyuk). After winning nearly one million dollars in the lottery, one might assume his life
warm.author: A Alcazar
warm.body:
Some people might believe that money is the solution to every problem; however, it hasn’t been like that for Gong Eun Tae ( Lee Jun Hyuk ). After winning nearly one million dollars in the lottery, one might assume his life will be completely changed; only it wasn’t like that. As it turns out, securing a hefty amount of money in your account doesn’t immediately warrant an easy path ahead, and in last week’s episodes we get to see how much more complicated things turn out when you win “ The Ordinary Jackpot .”
Set up more like a trap than an opportunity to show his abilities, Eun Tae, along with Jang Hyang Eun (Baek Yae In), has no choice but to be relentless while auditing another sales team. Although it doesn’t look easy, Eun Tae seems to have a plan to get exactly what he wants. In hindsight, the way he knows how to hit the nail on the head is both impressive and scary. He can measure both wins and losses, but that doesn’t mean he can always see the whole picture and the consequences of his actions.
When he effectively uncovers the corruption behind the sales team, it feels like both a victory and a defeat. He is doing the right thing by exposing the situation, and the people involved are by no means blameless victims. However, this shows that not everyone is completely black or white. As the sales team members aren’t heinous criminals, Eun Tae isn’t perfect either, nor is he completely on the right. Everything has different perspectives, and the way this show presents that is something worth noting.

warm.author: Chris Willman
warm.body:
When do trimmings become the main course? Or, to pose it in employment terms: When does a side hustle became the real hustle? And can that just go down without a hitch?
These are just ways into trying to think about developments in the career of Hayley Williams , who easily sold out two shows this week at the Hollywood Bowl , something we wouldn’t necessarily have taken for granted for her as a solo artist even a couple of years ago. In the first of two nights there Monday, Williams performed for almost exactly two hours without doing a single Paramore song — and what’s remarkable is, nobody cared.
Well, maybe that’s an overstatement: Probably someone out there in the full house of 17,000 had read the promo material for the tour and figured the promise of material from her three solo albums “plus exciting surprises” at least left room for the possibility of a Paramore or tune or two. But the “exciting surprises” on Monday amounted to a Portishead cover and a surprise encore appearance by Zedd, as opposed to “That’s What You Get.” Which was fine. More than fine, really: Williams’ Bowl set made for one of the most satisfying rock shows you could see this year, regardless of the fact that the only misery business being transacted was the unusually sweltering October weather that had everyone present walking up in a sweat.
Speaking of boiling, this all boils down to: What a difference a single album can make. For Williams, that album was 2025’s “Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party,” which she originally dribbled out in mysterious spurts like it was a bunch of between-project demos before everyone gradually realized that it added up to the game-changer project of her career. warm.body:
Drake reportedly didn't submit any music for 2027 Grammy consideration.
The 6 God's beef with the Grammys continues as another year passes with the Toronto rap star silently boycotting the storied award show. Sources tell Billboard that Drake has not officially submitted any music to The Recording Academy again this year, including his May albums Iceman, Habibti and Maid of Honour.
Drake has had a complicated relationship with the Grammys since criticizing the award show in 2017. In the years since then, it's been a crapshoot whether Drake will put his music in the running. He last submitted music in 2024, including the 21 Savage collab album Her Loss. Drake last won a Grammy Award in 2023 for Best Melodic Rap Performance for his contribution to Future's "Wait for U" featuring Tems.
2027 Grammy Award nominations will be announced on Nov. 16. The ceremony will take place on Feb. 7, 2027.
Despite Grammy Award wins apparently not being in Drake's future, he is setting up for a big 2027. Last month, he announced he will be heading out on tour next year to promote his three new albums, Iceman , Habibti and Maid of Honour .
"Obviously, a tour is coming, and there is other things on the horizon," he said during a recent interview. "Some big shows. We'll be out in 2027 to see everybody again across the world."
Drake is also rumored to be headlining the Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival in 2027.

The War on Drugs ’ keyboardist Robbie Bennett has two new albums dropping before the year is up. Both Steloken and Circulation will arrive on December 11 via American Dreams , adding 29 new tracks in total to Bennett’s solo catalog. Yesterday, he shared one song from each album; listen to “Sister” (from Steloken ) and “The Light on Your Face” (from Circulation ) below.
Both albums follow Bennett’s 2020 solo debut, Permanent World . He developed each track using the same keyboard he plays in the War on Drugs, but made them by sending MIDI from an acoustic player piano into an Oberheim OB-X8 synthesizer, permitting both instruments to play at once. He later incorporated layers of Fender Rhodes, vocoder, and Soma Terra, a “polyphonic microtonal synthesizer with a gyroscope and pressure-sensitive sensors.” “I want the music to be like you’re walking through an unfamiliar place you want to keep exploring and never have to circle back to where you started,” Bennett said in press materials.
Last month, Bennett also featured on the War on Drugs’ first new song since 2022, “ Who’s That .” The band hasn’t released a solo record since 2021’s I Don’t Live Here Anymore , but they did return with their second career live album, aptly titled Live Drugs Again , in 2024.

cold.headline: Live Nation hit with class action lawsuits over data breach involving Social Security numbers and health records
cold.kicker: Live Nation's statement came five days after Ticketmaster customers across the US ran into problems with ticket transfers. Source
cold.author: Mandy Dalugdug
cold.body:
Live Nation has been hit with at least three proposed class action lawsuits over a data breach involving Social Security numbers, government ID numbers, and health records.
Amanda Fraga filed her complaint in the US District Court for the Central District of California on Tuesday (October 6), and Toby Gosman and Isiah Ramos filed theirs in the same court on Wednesday (October 7).
Fraga and Gosman say they are former Live Nation employees who gave the company their personal information in connection with their jobs. Ramos does not say he worked for Live Nation ; his complaint says he provided his information “in connection with obtaining services from” the company.
Live Nation reported the breach to the Vermont Attorney General ‘s office on October 1 , according to the office’s public log of security breach notices .
The three complaints, which MBW has reviewed, were filed by different law firms but are almost word-for-word identical.
Fraga , a resident of Brooklyn, New York, is represented by Scott Edelsberg of Edelsberg Law . Ramos , a resident of Champaign, Illinois, is represented by John J. Nelson of Milberg .
Gosman , a Minnesota resident, is represented by Kristen Lake Cardoso of Kopelowitz Ostrow .
The jurisdiction section of Gosman ‘s complaint nonetheless describes the plaintiff as “a citizen of New York,” the same wording used in Fraga’s complaint .
All three plaintiffs say they learned of the breach from an article they read online.

cold.headline: Man sentenced to prison and to repay $8million on slop royalties in first criminal bot streaming fraud case
cold.kicker: He uploaded thousands of AI-generated songs to streaming platforms, then had bots play them billions of times The post Man sentenced to prison and to repay $8million on slop royalties in first criminal bot streaming frau
cold.author: Liberty Dunworth
cold.body:
Assorted music streaming apps on an iPhone. CREDIT: hapabapa/Getty Images
A man has been handed a prison sentence and ordered to repay the $8million he made from slop royalties, as the first criminal bot streaming fraud case has gone to court.
The ruling comes following a 54-year-old man from North Carolina pleading guilty to defrauding streaming services earlier this year. He managed to get $8million worth of royalties by uploading thousands of AI -generated songs to streaming platforms, then getting bots to play the songs billions of times.
In 2024 he was arrested, seven years after he started to collect royalties from the fake streams. It was also reported by the Justice Department that his AI-generated songs had over 80.9billion combined streams on YouTube Music in just one month alone. That figure is nearly 10 times higher than Taylor Swift ’s stats from the same period.
It has now become the first criminal bot streaming fraud case on record, and the man has been handed down a prison sentence for 18 months – charged on one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud.
He must also serve two years of supervised release, and is required to repay just shy of $8.1million.
Man Gets 18 Months in First U.S. AI Music Streaming Fraud Case After $8M Royalty Scheme https://t.co/u32gz3uJa1
Law Commentary reports that the man’s criminal scheme was active between 2017 and 2024, and used as many as 10,000 bot accounts at once. He also reportedly used fake email addresses and illegally obtained debit cards to create accounts on streaming services, before using software to make them repeatedly stream the AI songs he uploaded.

cold.headline: Quavo, Offset May Be Asked to Testify in Takeoff's Mom's Lawsuit
cold.author: C. Vernon Coleman II
cold.body:
Quavo and Offset may reportedly be asked to testify in Takeoff 's mother's wrongful death settlement battle.
After Takeoff's mom, Titania Davenport, settled a wrongful death lawsuit last year with the venue where the rapper was killed, she has been in a battle with Takeoff's father, Kenneth Ball, over the payout. On Wednesday (Oct. 7), TMZ reported that court documents show that Davenport, who is Quavo's older sister, is trying to get the case seen in a Georgia court, while Ball wants the case to take place in Texas.
In court documents, Davenport insists that all relevant witnesses, who could include Quavo and Offset, live in the Georgia area and holding the case in Texas would force them to incur unneeded expenses.
In 2023, Davenport sued 810 Billiards & Bowling, the Houston event venue where Takeoff was shot and killed in 2022. She reached an undisclosed settlement with the company in 2025. However, Takeoff's father says he is entitled to half the money. Davenport insists Ball was never involved in Takeoff's life and is just now stepping in to try and get a payday. Now, it will be up to a judge to decide.
In related news, the Takeoff murder trial is finally slated to begin next month on Nov. 5. Patrick Xavier Clark has been charged with shooting and killing the rapper during a confrontation during a dice game outside 810 Billiards & Bowling. Police say Takeoff was an innocent bystander. Clark faces life in prison if found guilty.

cold.headline: Olivia Rodrigo shares “hard line” stance on using AI in music

cold.author: Max Pilley
cold.body:
Olivia Rodrigo has shared her firm stance on using AI in her music, saying she would “never” incorporate the technology into her work.
The pop star discussed the controversial topic in a new interview with The Hollywood Reporter , where she was asked directly whether she would ever use it during the creative process.
“I would never use AI in any of my music,” Rodrigo responded. “Absolutely no. Hard line on that.”
She did reveal that she and long-time producer Dan Nigro had played around with ideas once, explaining: “The closest I’d ever got is that once, me and Dan were like, ‘God, I wonder what ideas ChatGPT would have for an Olivia Rodrigo title.’ And they’re all fucking awful.”
Her comments come as debate around AI continues to intensify across the music industry.
Last month, Suno admitted using audio obtained from YouTube to train its AI models , amid a wider legal battle over whether copyrighted material can be used to train generative technology.
Artists including Jason Isbell have also filed a lawsuit against Suno , alleging that the platform generates music designed to evoke specific musicians’ identities and styles without their consent.
Elsewhere, Dr. Dre recently said he was “embracing” AI in music , comparing resistance to the technology with the initial scepticism that greeted drum machines and synthesisers.
Rodrigo’s comments arrive during a busy period for the singer following the release of her third album, ‘You Seem Pretty Sad For A Girl So In Love’ , in June.

cold.headline: Skillet’s John Cooper Lets the “Monster” Out
cold.kicker: For Skillet’s John Cooper, hard rock became his way to survive a personal tragedy. When he was 15, Cooper’s mother died after a three-year battle with cancer. A piano teacher and devoted singer in church, she encouraged
cold.author: Steve Appleford
cold.body:
For Skillet’s John Cooper, hard rock became his way to survive a personal tragedy.
When he was 15, Cooper’s mother died after a three-year battle with cancer. A piano teacher and devoted singer in church, she encouraged her son’s musical dreams despite raising him in a deeply religious home where rock music, or anything with drums, was forbidden. Even wearing black was demonized.
After his mother’s death in 1990, Cooper’s relationship with his father unraveled, and he was soon drawn to the music he’d been taught to avoid. It finally led him to the creation of Skillet, now one of Christian rock’s leading voices.
“I would say it was the biggest life altering thing that has happened to me,” Cooper says of grief and struggle he faced as a Memphis teenager. “It’s why we sing so many songs about fighting your demons and telling people that they matter.”
The singer-bassist is on the phone from a festival date in Indiana, where Skillet are on a bill with Daughtry, just one stop in a busy year that he’s determined to keep focused on his music. Skillet’s newest songs are on After the Storm , a hard-hitting heavy metal EP to be released October 2. The band has been performing its raging first single, “Scream,” since June.
“I want it to rock,” Cooper says. “I want to have energy. I used to always say I’d like for somebody to hear it and go, ‘Man, I want to listen to that in the gym!’ That’s how I grew up listening to rock music—when I started playing sports and working out and driving cars. I always think of rock music as being synonymous with adrenaline and energy.

cold.headline: Andrew Savage Launches New Band Iconic Fugues with “2025 Dream/2025 Blues”
cold.kicker: “I think it’s just amazing the way a fun guitar solo can draw a bit of sun out from behind the clouds”
cold.author: Hattie Lindert
cold.body:
Andrew Savage has a new band with a new song out today. The Parquet Courts frontman has launched the group Iconic Fugues with a two-pronged track that’s surely relatable to anyone who has a rose and a thorn of the past year. Check out “2025 Dream/2025 Blues” below.
According to a statement from Savage, “2025 Dream/2025 Blues” is “about a guy who wakes up from a dream only to be confronted with a series of increasingly consequential, harsh realities.” Despite that dire synopsis, he doesn’t see the song as a total bummer. “As I write this all out it sounds bleak, but I don’t find it to be a bleak song. I think it’s just amazing the way a fun guitar solo can draw a bit of sun out from behind the clouds.”
Iconic Fugues came together some time after Savage released his most recent solo album, Several Songs About Fire , in 2023. Although the group’s final form “is still being decided,” as Savage told Shaad Magazine this week, a recent performance by the Marseille-based band featured his Several Songs About Fire collaborator Dylan Hadley and Santiago Aldunate of the psych-rock band Hantayo.
“There’s a difference between a solo record and a band record that I can’t quite put my finger on, but it’s just one of those things that you know when you hear it,” he added to Shaad. “I’ve been in France for four years, in Marseille for almost three, and I’ve got people here…. My life has changed, and so the music has changed, and I guess I needed a new name to sort of inaugurate that change, you know?” Parquet Courts, he added, are “not active at the moment, but still a band.”

cold.headline: Seo Hyun Jin’s World Comes Crashing Down Amid A Downpour In “The Perfect Lie”

cold.author: MLim
cold.body:
MBC’s upcoming drama “The Perfect Lie” has unveiled new stills featuring Seo Hyun Jin in character!
Helmed by “You and Everything Else” director Jo Young Min, “The Perfect Lie” is a psychological thriller in which a man and a woman give completely opposite accounts of the same memory, clashing fiercely in their search for the truth.
Yoo Yeon Seok plays Min Joon Ho, a man known for telling the truth. Min Joon Ho is a cardiac surgeon and a father raising his son alone following the death of his wife.
Seo Hyun Jin plays Kang Ji Sun, a woman who insists that her version of events is the truth. An elementary school librarian and teacher, Kang Ji Sun goes beyond simply listening to what others say, carefully examining the intentions behind their words.
After going on a first date with Min Joon Ho, Kang Ji Sun becomes entangled in an unexpected incident. As the two offer conflicting accounts of what happened, their disagreement escalates into a tense confrontation over the truth.
The newly released stills capture Kang Ji Sun amid a heavy downpour as she struggles with a whirlwind of emotions. As she steps outside without an umbrella, she appears overwhelmed by the situation unfolding around her.
In another still, she sits in the driver’s seat of a car, staring out at the rain while deep in thought. What has happened to Kang Ji Sun, and how will the incident affect her increasingly tense relationship with Min Joon Ho?

cold.headline: Man Sentenced to Prison for Bot Streams of AI Songs
cold.kicker: Mike Smith is the first person to face federal charges for music streaming fraud
cold.author: Kiana Mickles
cold.body:
A North Carolina man has been sentenced to 18 months in prison for collecting millions in royalties from bot streams of AI-generated songs, reports Rolling Stone . He is the first person to face federal charges for music streaming fraud.
From 2017 to 2024, the musician Mike Smith used thousands of bots to stream his own music as well as AI-generated songs he purchased and uploaded. Smith later pled guilty for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, a charge that carried a maximum prison sentence of five years. His lawyers originally argued that he should only get probation for the crime, while federal prosecutors urged a sentence of at least 46 months. As part of his plea deal, Smith agreed to forfeit $8 million in streaming proceeds. In addition to the 18-month prison sentence, he will undergo two years of supervised release.
“By flooding music streaming platforms with automated bots in the place of consumers, and fake songs in the place of creativity, Smith robbed millions in royalty payments from genuine artists and their fans,” U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said in a press release . “This Office is committed to ensuring the integrity of all markets, and protecting the public from those who use super intelligence for fraud.” (According to Reuters , the U.S. Department of Justice has instructed employees to start using the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” based on a recent executive order signed by President Trump.)

cold.headline: Music streaming fraud inquiry launched by US Copyright Office
cold.kicker: Notice of inquiry arrives a day after Michael Smith sentenced to 18 months in prison Source
cold.author: Murray Stassen
cold.body:
The US Copyright Office ( USCO ) has launched a public inquiry into music streaming fraud.
The Office published a notice of inquiry in the Federal Register on Wednesday ( October 7 ), seeking information on how streaming fraud is carried out, its economic impact, and its relationship to AI-generated music.
Written comments are due by November 23 , with reply comments due by December 21 .
The inquiry follows a request from Scott Fitzgerald , the Republican US Representative for Wisconsin’s 5th District, who sits on the House Judiciary Committee .
His letter to the USCO , dated May 21 , opens by asking it to “examine the contributory effects of artificial intelligence (AI) in music streaming fraud, and the resulting effect on the music industry.”
“While there is nothing inherently wrong with using AI as a creative tool in music development, or the organic growth of AI-generated music, specifically, generative AI can serve as a catalyst for criminals to perpetrate streaming fraud,” wrote Fitzgerald .
Fitzgerald added: “When AI-generated outputs compete against human-made works, they divert money from a finite royalty pool that would otherwise be distributed to actual rights holders. If done fraudulently by bad actors deploying bots or other forms of manipulation, it represents a clear theft of the royalty pool.”
